concepts.label: vertex
concepts.gloss: A vertex is a forwarding realm (a physical or logical node) inside the fabric that hosts terminations, access points, adaptations, gate sets and circuit endpoints and is a constituent element of a fabric topology.
concepts.example: R1 — a vertex in 'the zeta-over-optical realm' that hosts span terminations (e.g. hep-A1-R1), offer-gateway-points (e.g. acp-A1-grd) and circuit-end-points (e.g. cxp-a1a3-R1).

concepts.label: span-cap-point
concepts.gloss: A span-cap-point is a termination owned by a single vertex that represents one physical/logical end of a span (link) and thereby terminates that span at the vertex.
concepts.example: hep-A1-R1 — the span-cap-point on vertex R1 that terminates the link span-A1-R1 at the R1 end.

concepts.label: shifting-span
concepts.gloss: A shifting-span is an adaptation located at a vertex that bridges or maps traffic from one tier/stream container into another (a bridging adaptation that enables cross-tier carriage at that vertex).
concepts.example: crr4/grd2 bridging at R1 — a shifting-span at R1 that adapts the grd2 stream into the crr4 container so grd2 traffic can traverse on the crr4 path.

concepts.label: offer-gateway-point
concepts.gloss: An offer-gateway-point (ACP) is an access point on a vertex through which a carriage-offer presents service to its users; the ACP is the specific interface or port the offer uses on that vertex.
concepts.example: acp-A1-grd — the offer-gateway-point on vertex A1 that the carriage-offer co-a1a3-grd2 would use to present grd access at A1.

concepts.label: carriage-offer
concepts.gloss: A carriage-offer is a named service offering that carries a particular qualified stream between vertices over the fabric, uses specific offer-gateway-points, and is realized by circuit-end-points on vertices.
concepts.example: co-a1a3-grd2 (grd2, A1 to A3) — a carriage-offer moving the grd2 stream from A1 to A3 that uses offer-gateway-points (e.g. acp-A1-grd, acp-A3-grd), is realized by circuit-end-points (cxp-a1a3-R1 and cxp-a1a3-R3), and runs over the zeta-over-optical fabric.

concepts.label: tier-stream-qualifier
concepts.gloss: A tier-stream-qualifier is a multiplexing label or stream identifier that qualifies which sub-stream (tier) a carriage-offer carries and which can be mapped into higher-level containers by shifting-spans.
concepts.example: grd2 mapped into crr4 — the tier-stream-qualifier 'grd2' being placed into the crr4 container so that offers can carry grd2 within the crr4 transport.

concepts.label: vertex-gate-set
concepts.gloss: A vertex-gate-set is a local switching resource (a set of cross-switch gates) resident on a vertex used to switch or route flows between local terminations, spans and access points.
concepts.example: R2 cross-switch gate set — the gate set at vertex R2 that controls switching between spans and offer/access points terminating at R2.

concepts.label: span
concepts.gloss: A span is a physical or logical link between two vertices inside the fabric; each span is terminated at its ends by one or more span-cap-points on the respective vertices.
concepts.example: span-A1-R1 — the link connecting vertex A1 and vertex R1, terminated at R1 by hep-A1-R1 (and at A1 by the corresponding span-cap-point on A1).

concepts.label: fabric
concepts.gloss: A fabric is the multi-tier topology or network realm that contains vertices and spans and over which carriage-offers and their realizations are provided.
concepts.example: the zeta-over-optical realm — the fabric containing vertices R1,R2,R3,A1,A2,A3 and spans such as span-R1-R2 and span-A1-R1 that carry offers like co-a1a3-grd2.

concepts.label: circuit-end-point
concepts.gloss: A circuit-end-point (CXP) is an endpoint on a vertex that constitutes part of the realization of a carriage-offer and represents one terminus of the offer's realized circuit at that vertex.
concepts.example: cxp-a1a3-R1 — the circuit-end-point on vertex R1 that, together with cxp-a1a3-R3, realizes the carriage-offer co-a1a3-grd2 between A1 and A3.
